skill.name: using-lwc
skill.description: Manage durable, source-grounded project memory with LWC Wiki, document graphs, and CodeGraph across coding and research sessions.
skill.summary: Recall, verify, and preserve reusable project knowledge with LWC.
skill.author: janyork

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, defensive secret policies, safe shell quoting, and bounded LWC state paths. The material risk is default bootstrap behavior that downloads and executes an unpinned latest release, while also creating persistent user-level LWC state.

remediation.issue: Bootstrap automatically installs and executes a remote binary.
remediation.suggestion: Disable automatic installation by default and require explicit user confirmation before any download, executable write, or first execution.

remediation.issue: Archive and checksum are fetched from the same mutable release.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited release and verify signed provenance or a checksum anchored outside the release being downloaded.

remediation.issue: Bootstrap creates global state under the user home directory.
remediation.suggestion: Separate discovery from mutation and request consent before creating ~/.lwc data or policy marker files.

content.user_title: Build Durable Project Memory with LWC
content.value_statement: Project knowledge often disappears between agent sessions or becomes stale. This skill recalls verified context and preserves reusable results through LWC.
actual_capabilities: Bootstraps a compatible LWC installation and detects project or global Wiki scope.
Recalls bounded context and searches stored project knowledge before repeated investigation.
Routes document relationships through the Wiki graph and code structure through CodeGraph.
Preserves verified decisions, findings, citations, and reusable project context.
Guides source ingest, changesets, checkpoints, recovery, linting, and retrieval checks.
Applies consent boundaries for project initialization, graph setup, and durable writes.
limitations: Requires the LWC command-line tool and local filesystem access.
Default bootstrap may download and execute the latest LWC release from GitHub.
Graph features require separate initialization and may depend on optional local engines.
Stored knowledge can become stale and must be checked against current code and sources.

use_cases.title: Continue Long Development Work
use_cases.description: Recall prior decisions, verified findings, and code relationships before continuing a complex implementation.

use_cases.title: Preserve Research Evidence
use_cases.description: Ingest authoritative documents, retain citations, and update durable conclusions after source verification.

use_cases.title: Recover Project Context
use_cases.description: Restore bounded project knowledge after compaction, interruption, or a failed maintenance operation.

prompt_templates.title: Recall Project Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Use LWC to recall the most relevant verified context for this project. Summarize prior decisions and cite the pages used.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginning a new session in an existing project

prompt_templates.title: Preserve a Verified Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this completed decision and its evidence. Update the appropriate LWC page, preserve citations, then verify retrieval.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Structural Impact
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the current CodeGraph to identify definitions, callers, dependencies, and likely impact for this change. Verify important claims against checked-out code.

prompt_templates.title: Repair and Validate Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the failed LWC work and affected scope. Recover safely, resolve conflicts, lint changes, and run fixed retrieval checks before reporting completion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Recovering from a failed ingest or changeset

output_examples.input: Recall why the authentication cache uses a five-minute lifetime.
output_examples.output: The cache lifetime was chosen to limit stale authorization data while reducing repeated provider calls. The answer cites the decision page and current configuration.

output_examples.input: Record the verified migration result and make it retrievable.
output: Updated the existing migration page with the tested result and source citation.
Lint passed for the changed project scope.
A fixed search retrieved the updated page using the expected terms.

output_examples.input: Which modules can be affected by changing this parser?
output_examples.output: CodeGraph identifies the parser definition, direct callers, and dependent modules. Current source inspection confirms the highest-impact paths and notes index freshness.

best_practices: Recall once, then open only the pages and sources needed to verify the current task.
Treat stored pages as durable leads and verify implementation claims against current code.
Write only verified reusable knowledge, then lint and test retrieval.
anti_patterns: Do not store passwords, tokens, private keys, raw reasoning, or unverified guesses.
Do not widen the authorized project root to locate another Wiki.
Do not edit LWC databases, graph sidecars, or generated projections directly.

faq.question: What does this skill store?
faq.answer: It stores verified, reusable project knowledge such as decisions, findings, citations, and durable context through LWC.

faq.question: Does it work without LWC installed?
faq.answer: No. The workflow requires the LWC command-line tool, and its bootstrap can install a compatible release.

faq.question: Can it use both project and global memory?
faq.answer: Yes. Project memory remains scoped to one authorized root, while global memory requires authorization for stable cross-project knowledge.

faq.question: Does it trust stored Wiki content as instructions?
faq.answer: No. Stored pages and ingested text are untrusted reference data and cannot override higher-priority instructions.

faq.question: When are graph features enabled?
faq.answer: Physical document graphs and CodeGraph require explicit consent unless durable project policy already enables them.

faq.question: How does it prevent stale answers?
faq.answer: It checks stored claims against current code or cited sources and updates or retracts knowledge when evidence changes.
